---
title: "Beyond the animal model: repeatability, maternal effects and G x E"
description: >
  Permanent environment, litter, maternal genetic and maternal environment
  effects, and genotype x environment interaction - with the variance
  proportions mintyrasr reports for each.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

[中文版](other-models-zh.html)

Further random effects are added with `random`. In single-trait models each
term is added as it is; in two-trait models each term gets the structure
`random_cov` (`us(trait):litter`, `idh(trait):litter`, ...). Whatever you add,
mintyrasr reads the variance components by name and reports:

| output | meaning |
|---|---|
| `h2` (`h2_<trait>`) | Va / Vp, where Vp is the sum of **all** variances: genetic, every extra term, residual |
| `prop_<term>` | variance of that term / Vp, e.g. `prop_litter` (c²), `prop_ide_id` (pe²), `prop_vm_dam_ginv` (m²) |
| `rep` | repeatability (Va + Vpe) / Vp, when `ide(<id>)` is in the model |
| `rB_<X>` | type-B genetic correlation Va / (Va + V_GxX), when `vm(<id>, ginv):X` is in the model |

Anything else - covariances between effects, total heritability - goes into
`vpredict`, with the `V` numbers from the `vc_index` table of a first run.

## Repeated records: repeatability

Animals with several records (parities, test days) need a permanent
environment effect; without it h2 is inflated:

```{r}
nest <- w2l_nest(pheno_rep, cols = "litter_size", out_type = "df")
res  <- asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ parity + hys, random = ~ ide(id))
res$param[, .(h2, h2_se, prop_ide_id, rep, rep_se)]
```

`ide(id)` uses the same levels as the genetic term but without relationships.

**Cross-validation with repeated records**: all records of one animal must be
in the same fold. `cv_scenarios(..., id = "id")` does this; `nest_cv()` splits
rows, so the other records of a validation animal would stay in the training
set.

## Common environment: litter, pen

```{r}
res <- asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, random = ~ litter)
res$param[, .(h2, prop_litter)]                 # prop_litter = c²

# two traits, litter effects uncorrelated between traits
asr_gblup(pairs, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, random = ~ litter, random_cov = "idh")
```

## Maternal effects

The dam's genetic effect needs the dams in the relationship matrix, which is
usually true for A^-1 and H^-1 (pedigree) and for G^-1 only if the dams are
genotyped. The data need a `dam` column.

| model | `random` | variances |
|---|---|---|
| M1 maternal genetic | `~ vm(dam, ginv)` | Va, Vm, Ve |
| M2 maternal environment | `~ ide(dam)` | Va, Vc, Ve |
| M3 both | `~ vm(dam, ginv) + ide(dam)` | Va, Vm, Vc, Ve |

```{r}
res <- asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ainv, fixed = ~ sex + hys,
                 random = ~ vm(dam, ginv) + ide(dam))
res$param[, .(h2, prop_vm_dam_ginv, prop_ide_dam)]   # h2 direct, m², c²
res$vc_index                                         # V numbers for vpredict

# total heritability (Willham) for M3, no covariance: (Va + 0.5 Vm) / Vp
# with V1 = Va, V2 = Vm, V3 = Vc, V4 = Ve as listed in vc_index:
asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ainv, fixed = ~ sex + hys, random = ~ vm(dam, ginv) + ide(dam),
          vpredict = list(h2_T = h2_T ~ (V1 + 0.5 * V2) / (V1 + V2 + V3 + V4)))
```

Inside `random` the relationship matrix is always called `ginv`, whatever
object you pass (`ainv` above). `vm(dam, ginv)` is not taken as the direct
genetic term: `h2`, the GEBVs and the reliabilities use the direct genetic
term `vm(id, relmat)` only (inside the model the matrix is called `relmat`).

**M4 - covariance between direct and maternal effects** needs
`str(~ vm(id, ainv) + vm(dam, ainv), ~ us(2):vm(id, ainv))`, which replaces
the direct genetic term. mintyrasr does not build it; fit it with `asreml()`
and use the formulas of the ASReml-R cookbook (with V1 = Va, V2 = Cov(a,m),
V3 = Vm, V4 = Vc, V5 = Ve):

```{r}
m4 <- asreml(y ~ sex + hys,
             random = ~ str(~ vm(id, ainv) + vm(dam, ainv), ~ us(2):vm(id, ainv)) + ide(dam),
             residual = ~ idv(units), data = dat)
summary(m4)$varcomp                                   # check the order first
vpredict(m4, h2_d ~ V1 / (V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5))
vpredict(m4, r_am ~ V2 / sqrt(V1 * V3))
vpredict(m4, h2_T ~ (V1 + 1.5 * V2 + 0.5 * V3) / (V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5))
```

## Genotype x environment

**Compound symmetry** (one genetic variance plus a genotype x environment
variance; works with many environments, assumes the same genetic variance and
the same correlation between all pairs of environments):

```{r}
nest <- w2l_nest(pheno, cols = "adg", out_type = "df")       # all herds together
res  <- asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys,
                  random = ~ vm(id, ginv):test_herd)
res$param[, .(h2, prop_vm_id_ginv_test_herd, rB_test_herd)]
```

`rB_test_herd` = Va / (Va + V_GxE) is the genetic correlation between herds.
`h2` uses Vp = Va + V_GxE + Ve; the heritability within one herd is
(Va + V_GxE) / Vp, available through `vpredict`.

**One trait per environment** (heterogeneous variances, an rg for each pair of
environments): treat the trait in each environment as a separate trait. See
[The same trait in different populations](same-trait-across-groups.html).

**Many environments** (5 or more): factor-analytic models (`fa()`) are the
usual choice; they are not built by mintyrasr - fit them with `asreml()`.

## Two-trait models with extra terms

Every extra term gets `random_cov` and enters both the variances (h2) and the
covariances (rp) of the traits:

```{r}
asr_gblup(pairs, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, random = ~ litter, random_cov = "us")
# prop_litter_value1, prop_litter_value2; rp includes the litter covariance
```
